disposition_reason: The 1st HKTDS reports food-item means and ranges for 'Chocolate' (4 composites, March 2010-February 2011) for Al, Cd, Pb, Ni and Sn (plus Sb and V, not tracked). Chocolate was not in the 51-item methylmercury panel; arsenic and total mercury are not in this report.

study.sampling_unit: composite samples of 3 purchased samples per occasion (one composite per occasion)
study.method: Closed-vessel microwave digestion in concentrated HNO3; high-resolution ICP-MS (CFS Food Research Laboratory)
study.basis: as consumed (TDS food prepared in form normally consumed; chocolate eaten as purchased), wet weight

notes: Untracked analytes for chocolate: antimony mean 6 µg/kg (3-14) and vanadium 40 µg/kg (15-71). Food-group rows 'Sugars and confectionery' (8 composites: chocolate + granulated white sugar) are mixed and not extracted. Report text (para 8.5) ranks chocolate (mean 1400 µg/kg) third-highest for nickel after peanut and peanut butter. No out-of-scope chocolate-containing composite foods are listed as TDS items in this report.
contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary sets sampling_year_range null although the primary states March 2010-February 2011 (paras 2.2/Executive summary).
Stored summary lists MeHg among metals; chocolate was not analysed for MeHg (only 51 mainly animal-origin items).
unresolved: Per-item percentage <LOD for chocolate is not printed; the 1/2 LOD treatment of means is inferred from all-ND items rather than stated in the Appendix table notes.
Al ranges (4.0-19 mg/kg) all exceed the LOQ; other analytes likewise; no below-LOQ flagging is printed.
